name: pick_ledger
question: do the operator's own stock picks beat simply holding the index? His two large real-money gains (months-long holds in single names) are the only edge in this project with a real-money record, and two wins in a rising market prove nothing.
tool: tools/pick_ledger.py; ledger docs/pick_ledger.jsonl, committed after every add (git history is the proof of order)
what_counts_as_a_pick: a symbol recorded with `add` BEFORE its entry: stamped with the record time, thesis, intended hold and a sell condition. A repeat of the same symbol within 10 calendar days is refused. A pick recorded after the fact (--retro) is listed and never scored. Picks are scored whether or not real money was put on them.
entry_exit: entry = the open of the first session starting after the record time; exit for scoring = the open 21 / 63 / 126 sessions later (adjusted prices); a name that stops trading is sold at its last close. The pick is scored at the horizon whether or not the operator still holds it.
measure: ratio lift (1 + pick) / (1 + control) - 1. Control A = SPY over the same sessions. Control B = the mean of 30 random names from the liquid list (close >= $10, 20-day dollar volume >= $20M), seeded by the pick id.
primary: 63 sessions, on the FIRST 30 scoreable picks in record order, read once when all 30 have a closed window. Later picks never enter this verdict.
pass: mean ratio lift vs SPY > 0 AND t across the 30 picks >= 2.0 AND more than half the picks ahead of SPY AND the median pick ahead of SPY AND mean lift vs the random names > 0.
fail: anything else. No second sample for the same question without a new prereg.
reported_not_verdict: open windows marked to the latest open
the best single pick's share of the total (the ride-the-trend test on 11/11 showed the top 1% of trades making more than the whole profit)
caveats: 30 picks give low power: only a large skill shows up. A FAIL means not shown, not disproven.
picks made in one market regime share that regime; t across picks overstates the evidence if they cluster in time or in one sector.
this takes at least 3 months after the 30th pick.
it measures PICKING, not what the operator would have earned: his own entries, sizes and exits are not modelled.
nothing here places an order or recommends one.
skeptic: round 1 on 11/11 (NOT READY: 3 blockers, 5 majors, 4 minors); every finding applied before any pick was recorded, see amended_after_skeptic_round_1

amended_after_skeptic_round_1.proof_of_order: each ledger line carries the id of the line before it and an id computed from its own content (hash chain); `add` commits the line itself; `score` refuses a damaged chain and scores a pick only if its line's first git commit is earlier than its entry open. Picks are recorded on the MacBook (which can push).
amended_after_skeptic_round_1.sample: the first 30 COUNTABLE picks in record order. Retro picks, funds / levered products, and picks recorded after 2027-11-11 never count. If any of the 30 cannot be scored (never committed, committed late, no entry bar, stock type unknown) or lacks its random-name control or beta, the verdict is BLOCKED; it is never replaced by pick 31. Fewer than 30 by 2027-11-11 = UNPROVEN.
amended_after_skeptic_round_1.one_pick_per_symbol: per 92 calendar days (about 63 sessions), so one name cannot fill the sample inside one window.
amended_after_skeptic_round_1.control_B: 30 names drawn at `add` time (seeded by the line's id) from docs/studies/pick_ledger_universe.txt, a list of 1,931 liquid common stocks FROZEN on 2026-11-11 from the 2026-10-15 table, before any pick; the 30 names are stored in the ledger line. Being fixed before every pick, the list has no look-ahead; a control name that later stops trading is valued at its last close.
amended_after_skeptic_round_1.pass: ALL of: mean ratio lift vs SPY > 0; t >= 2.0 with picks clustered by entry month (at least 4 months); more than half the picks ahead of SPY; median ahead of SPY; mean ratio lift vs the 30 random names > 0; mean rank of the pick among its own 30 controls above the 50th percentile; mean beta-adjusted excess (pick - beta x SPY, beta from the 252 sessions before entry) > 0.
amended_after_skeptic_round_1.power: an estimate, not a measurement: with a 20-25% standard deviation of 63-session excess return across picks, 30 picks have about 80% power only for an average edge near +10 to +13% per pick per quarter. This test can show a large skill; it cannot rule out a modest one.
known_soft_spots: a name that goes bankrupt is valued at its last exchange close, which overstates it (flagged in the output)
the operator can see running numbers for open picks; that is unavoidable for his own positions and is why the sample is fixed by record order and has an end date
beta from 252 prior sessions is missing for a recent listing; such a pick blocks the verdict until the prereg is amended in writing

amended_2026-11-11_early_look: Operator 11/11: May 2027 is too long to wait. Added an EARLY LOOK at 21 sessions on the SAME first 30 countable picks, read once when all 30 have a closed 21-session window (about late February to March 2027). Same pass conditions as the 63-session verdict, with the clustered t raised to 2.5 because it is a second look at the same picks. It is weaker evidence than the 63-session verdict (one month is a noisy test of a multi-month idea) and does not replace it: an early PASS followed by a 63-session FAIL is a FAIL. Written before any pick was recorded in this ledger.
